education.title: Phishing
education.body: Fake emails or websites that copy a real bank or company to trick you into entering your details. Check the web address carefully — type it yourself instead of following links.
education.tip: Never sign in from a link in a message. Open your browser and type the address.

education.title: Smishing (SMS phishing)
education.body: Fraudulent SMS or WhatsApp messages claiming your account is blocked, or that you have won a prize. Banks never ask for OTPs, PINs or passwords by message.
education.tip: Call your bank using the number on the back of your card — never a number in the message.

education.title: Fake banking messages
education.body: Screenshots of fake 'payment proofs' or 'EFT notifications'. Money can appear to reflect and later be reversed.
education.tip: Wait until the money has cleared and is truly available before delivering goods.

education.title: Investment scams
education.body: 'Double your money' schemes on WhatsApp and social media. Guaranteed returns and pressure to recruit friends are warning signs.
education.tip: Legitimate investments never guarantee profits. Check with the FSCA before investing.

education.title: Job scams
education.body: 'Earn R5,000 per day from home' offers that ask for a joining fee or your banking details upfront.
education.tip: A real employer never asks you to pay to get a job.

education.title: Social engineering
education.body: Someone builds trust — posing as a bank agent, a family member in trouble, or a romantic partner — to get money or information.
education.tip: Verify the person through a channel you trust before sending anything.

quiz.q: Your 'bank' SMS asks you to confirm your OTP to stop a suspicious payment. What do you do?
options: Send the OTP quickly so they can block it
Do nothing — real banks never ask for your OTP — and call the bank using the number on your card
Reply asking if they are really the bank
quiz.explain: Anyone with your OTP can move your money. Banks never ask for it by message or phone.

quiz.q: A WhatsApp job ad offers R4,500 per day, but you must pay a R250 'registration fee' first. This is…
options: Probably legitimate if they have a logo
A scam — real jobs never ask you to pay first
quiz.explain: Pay-first offers are one of the most common job scams in South Africa.

quiz.q: Which of these is the safest way to check if a message from your bank is real?
options: Tap the link in the message to check
Call your bank using the number on your card or official app
Reply to the message asking for proof
quiz.explain: Always verify through an official channel you find yourself.
